simple.meaning: סְבַל (çᵉbal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to erect.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across Ezra, beginning at Ezra 6:3. Its contexts include sacrifice, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְבַל (H5446).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H5446. sebal [ סְבַל ] verb si vera lectio bear, carry a load (see Biblical Hebrew); — Po`. Passive participle מְסוֺבְלִים אֻשֹּׁ֫הִי (K § 36 Nö GGA, 1884, 1016 ) Ezra 6:3 its foundations (be) raised (Thes and others; W CG 203, 225 ), very dubious; Hpt Gu on the passage conjectures ׳אֶשֹּׁהִ ׳מְס his (God's) fire-offerings they bring (Assyrian Zabâlu ), so (hesitantly) Berthol.

occurrences.englishText: In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: Concerning God’s house at Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be strongly laid; with its height sixty cubits,* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. and its width sixty cubits;
